cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Don’t Go
cards.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll finish your packing. Give me the jam jar and I'll wrap it properly before you close the case.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper. I need to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good thinking. I'll tuck the sleeves round the lid; just check the glass with me so we know it won't leak.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather leave the jar here than open the case again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sensible. I'll look after it. Have one taste from a spoon before you decide it's mine to keep; you can tell me whether I should save you another jar.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asserts packing competence and A3 endorses B jumper solution; A5 adapts leaving jam into taste, but B4 refusing case reopening conflicts with leaving a packed jar.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 wrapping constructively; A5 uses B4 leaving jar, yet the case-open state is unclear and leaving it would itself require access if already packed.

relationship.evidence: B2 departure need plausible; B4 solution has a practical inconsistency about avoiding reopening while removing jar.

heightening.evidence: A5 taste-before-gift is a relevant indirect delay once jar accessible, but access needs coherent setup.

specificity.evidence: A1 before closing case and B4 open case again imply a closure that never enters clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 lengthy offer is otherwise speakable; case-state confusion is avoidable.
